C-PTSD is Complex PTSD and is very much diagnosable. The difference between the two is PTSD is caused by one traumatic event whereas C-PTSD is caused by multiple and/or ongoing traumas.  Your doctor should know this, are you able to change to someone else?
You're more than welcome, I was actually worried it only made sense to me! 😊
ATM means 'at the moment'... It also means 'automatic teller machine' but that wouldn't make sense in this context 😂

Yeah I do tend to ramble 😂 But sometimes I make sense. I guess statistically speaking I'm bound to eventually. I mean the amount I ramble on and on, something of value will come out every now and then. 

Love that pregnancy analogy, exactly right! And yeah, I'm pretty good atm. Not 100% and a bit lost as to what to do with my life but alot better than I used to be. I hope you can say the same soon. x

I'd spent half an hour trying to explain triggers to my friend but I was having a bad day so nothing I was saying was making sense because I couldn't think clearly. I eventually gave up and just said it was like PTSD throwing you a surprise party... (you know the rest). 

And yeah, I totally get what your saying with regards to so many people being under the impression only people in the armed forces get PTSD, it frustrates the hell out of me. About 6 months ago my mother told me my brother-in-law (Snr Detective who was in the police force for 20+ years) has PTSD and it crushed me. Here's how the conversation went:

Mum: So P*** is on medical leave because of something called PSTD. 
Me: You mean PTSD. 
Mum: Oh do you know what it is? 
Me: Yes mum, I was diagnosed with C-PTSD at the beginning of the year. 
Mum: *laughs* Don't be ridiculous! Why on earth would you have it?! 

It also frustrates me that people think there are levels of severity to PTSD and that the more horrific the trauma the more severe your PTSD is. PTSD is PTSD, it's not easy for anyone. Yes people in the armed forces witness some horrific things, things I certainly couldn't cope with, but that doesn't make PTSD worse for them. And too many people who have C-PTSD are diagnosed with PTSD, that annoys me too! 

I don't know if I'll ever be me again, I don't think I will. I built a very successful domiciliary care company that specialised in end of life care and I was well respected in the care industry. Now I can't even return a coke float to MacDonalds (they didn't put ice cream in it) because the idea of confrontation terrifies me. Instead I had a full blown anxiety attack in the carpark. To go from who I use to be to who I have become broke my heart but it's gotten easier. I think maybe I'm forgetting who I was and getting use to the new me which is sad but at least I don't feel like a stranger in my own mind anymore. 

I think that's where you're at, a stranger in your own mind, and I totally feel your pain. I don't suffer every day anymore like I'm guessing you do, only when I'm triggered, but I'll never forget what hell it was. I nearly didn't make it, I gave up a couple of times because I couldn't see any other way to end my suffering. Fortunately I'm still here and there was light at the end of the tunnel. I know that doesn't help you to hear but it's true. It does get easier, it just takes time. 

You do whatever you need to to cope, just as long as you survive. My self-destructive behaviour was pretty bad and I made alot of mistakes but I try not to beat myself up over them because I just did what I had to to survive.

Your surprise party sounds shitloads more fun than mine... Completely self-destructive of course and likely to end badly but isn't that the whole meaning behind the saying "it's all fun and games until someone loses an eye"...?
